raw_summary: Equine chiropractors and bodyworkers across rodeo, ranch, and performance circuits emphasize whole-horse mobility and compensation-pattern detection. Recurring topics center on gait dysfunction, post-travel stiffness, and hind-end issues (especially sacroiliac adjustments), with strong rodeo-specific positioning around horse conditioning, bucking stock recovery, and performance restoration. Content hooks leverage "before/after" proof and early-detection messaging, often reframing performance problems as structural misalignment rather than training or tack issues. Visual strategy relies on clinical close-ups of hand techniques, gait video comparisons, and dramatic reaction shots. Practitioners frequently blend chiropractic with complementary modalities (massage, myofascial release, kinesiology taping, cellular therapy). Montana and Texas markets show particular overlap of rodeo professionals, ranch horse specialists, and mobile practitioners.
